explanation: The isometric case: X is a connected Riemannian manifold whose (e)metric is the Riemannian distance (IsRiemannianManifold), G locally compact acting continuously, faithfully, by isometries. By Myers–Steenrod the isometry group is a Lie group; a continuous injective homomorphism of a locally compact G into a Lie group forces G to have no small subgroups, hence G is Lie by Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin/Yamabe. This is a correct known special case (a sub-case of the Lipschitz case of Repovš–Ščepin mentioned on Wikipedia, Hilbert–Smith conjecture). The connected metrizable manifold is automatically second countable, so no edge cases. Faithful.
